statuses.title: Per-group adaptive clip sync reduces group counts positionally, so an empty rank receives permuted counts and thresholds diverge
statuses.note: Fix commit 23521ab6 (#888). The collective schedule is now schema-derived at both levels. (a) sync: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_distributed.py:64-71 pins `group_names = sorted(current_pg.values)` off `_current_clipping_norm` and indexes `state._num_clipped[gname]`, so the i-th reduce_scalar is bound to a key, not a dict position; the threshold loop at :78 reuses the same list. (b) every construction site of the per-group count dict is canonicalized: _adaptive.py:397 (`dict.fromkeys(sorted(initial_clipping_norm.values), 0.0)`), :483-487 (return_stats empty), :538-556 and :584 (the two non-empty branches build over `sorted(current_pg.values)`), _clipped_fun.py:248-250, :329-331, :343-348, _clipped_grad.py:269-271. I grepped every `num_clipped` / `dict.fromkeys` site in opaque-engine/opaque-dpsgd/opaque-dpftrl sources; none is left unsorted. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: (1) a 40-step 2-rank gloo run of the real stack (PoissonSampler -> adaptive_clipped_grad(PerGroup) -> sum_gradients -> sync -> gaussian_noise) with a non-sorted, non-leaf PerGroup order ({zzz:1.0, aaa:1000.0} over leaves [zzz_w, aaa_b]; sorted order ('aaa','zzz') differs from both) produced 9 partially-empty and 3 fully-empty rounds and ended with byte-identical thresholds and identical `_num_clipped` key order ('aaa','zzz') on both ranks; (2) a DISCRIMINATING control: I re-implemented the pre-#888 positional loop in-process and permuted rank 1's `_num_clipped` dict -- legacy DIVERGES (rank0 zzz=0.904837 vs rank1 zzz=1.105171) while the current `sync_adaptive_clip_state` agrees, proving the sync itself (not only the upstream ordering) is order-insensitive; (3) the shipped regression `packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/ddp/test_dpsgd_cpu_gloo.py::test_per_group_adaptive_clipping_one_rank_empty_syncs` runs on 2 real gloo ranks with one empty rank, asserts `tuple(bounds.values) == ('weight','bias')` (non-sorted) and all_gather_objects the thresholds. It is `pytestmark = pytest.mark.distributed`, so the PR/main distributed lane (`-m 'distributed and not cuda'`, no slow exclusion) executes it.

statuses.title: Per-group clipping crashes DDP training on any partially-empty Poisson round
statuses.note: Fix commit e8568596 (#875). Aux `clipping_rate` presence is now a function of the clipping schema: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py:245 emits `clipping_rate=None if isinstance(clipping_norm, PerGroup) else 0.0` on the empty-batch short-circuit, and packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:465 does the same (`None if is_per_group else 0.0`). `_sync_clipping_rate` (engine/clipping/_distributed.py:233-249) still issues exactly two presence reduces plus two value reduces on every rank, so the schedule is fixed. I probed ALL SIBLING PATHS the fix did not explicitly name: clipped_grad / auto_clipped_grad / adaptive_clipped_grad x {PerGroup, scalar} x {plain, microbatch_size=2, second_moment=True} -- 12 combinations, every one with matching `clipping_rate` presence between a 3-example batch and an empty batch (PerGroup -> None/None, scalar -> float/float). The `clipped_fun` sibling reaches the same answer structurally: _clipped_fun.py:780-784 collapses a dict rate to None and _compute_clipping_stats returns a dict for PerGroup on both the empty (:328-336) and non-empty (:343-355) branches. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION on real 2-rank gloo: my own 40-step end-to-end run (fixed PerGroup clipped_grad + PoissonSampler + sum_gradients + sync(aux) + gaussian_noise) survived 9 partially-empty and 3 fully-empty rounds with no `clipping_rate presence mismatch`; the shipped `packages/opaque-engine/tests/ddp/test_sync_aux_empty_batch.py::test_per_group_clipped_grad_one_rank_empty_does_not_desync` (slow+distributed, added by the same commit) drives the REAL `clipped_grad(PerGroup, return_aux=True)` on both ranks rather than hand-built auxes, which was the OPQ-331 fix sketch's requirement; and `test_sync_schema_contracts_preserve_collective_parity` still proves the presence check is discriminating (`pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='clipping_rate presence mismatch')`). The older hand-built helper `_worker_sync_aux_empty_vs_per_group` (engine_ddp_helpers.py:672-716) was NOT rebuilt through the real path, but it is now redundant rather than load-bearing.

findings.title: DDP resume collapses every rank's Poisson sampler stream to rank 0's, so co-indexed records across shards are perfectly co-included while the accountant still prices independent Poisson
findings.line: 1871-1877 (restore on every rank), 3945-3950 (per-rank fold, fresh runs only), 5195-5197 + 5279-5284 (snapshot written only where should_save is true), 3878-3885 (the acknowledging comment)
findings.claim: Under DDP the trainer shards the dataset per rank and folds the rank into the sampler key (`sampler_key = fold_in(sampler_key, self._ddp.rank)`, _dp_trainer.py:3949) precisely so each rank draws an INDEPENDENT Bernoulli(q) mask over its shard -- that independence is what makes the union of the shard draws an exact Poisson sample of the whole population, which is the hypothesis `acc.poisson` prices (_dp_trainer.py:1492 'The accountant uses regular ``acc.poisson`` over the global rate'). The sampler snapshot, however, is written ONLY by the saving rank (`_save_dp_runtime` is inside `if _distributed.should_save(...)`, _dp_trainer.py:5195-5197, default world-rank-0) and is restored by EVERY rank (`ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)`, :1875-1877). Every sampler family restores the stream key straight out of the snapshot (`stream_key=RngKey(seed=int(sd['key_seed']), ...)`: dpsgd/_poisson.py:261, dpsgd/_k_out_of_t.py:218, dpftrl/_poisson.py:304, dpftrl/_b_min_sep.py:259, dpftrl/_balls_in_bins.py:260), so after a resume all W ranks replay rank 0's stream and select the SAME LOCAL OFFSETS in their disjoint shards. Records that happen to share a local index across shards are then included or excluded together with probability 1, for the rest of training. The in-file comment at :3869-3873 asserts the opposite -- 'the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected' -- which is false: Poisson amplification needs independence across records, not just the right marginal.
findings.failure_scenario: torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 (or 4/8) with the default save_strategy='steps'; the job is preempted and restarted with resume_from_checkpoint. REPRODUCED END TO END on a real 2-rank gloo DPTrainer run (TinyForCausalLM, 16 examples, per_device_train_batch_size=2, save_steps=2, resume from checkpoint-2): fresh run stream keys were rank0=1950457451192556855, rank1=16528425509808239245 (independent); after resume BOTH ranks reported 1950457451192556855 -- rank 0's key -- on every step. Confirmed at the sampler level too: two PoissonSamplers seeded with fold_in(key(42),0)/fold_in(key(42),1) emit different index lists ([[4,5,8],[1,5,9,14,15],...] vs [[3,5,7,13,15],[0,6],...]); after both are rebuilt through `from_state_dict` with rank 0's snapshot they emit byte-identical lists. QUANTIFIED: with sigma=1.0, q=0.01, delta=1e-5, a single step of the intended independent Poisson mechanism has eps = 0.1995 (numerically integrated hockey-stick on the standard dominating pair N(0) vs (1-q)N(0)+qN(1)). The neighbouring pair actually realised by W=2 correlated groups -- D={w}, D'={w,z} where w and z share one Bernoulli, i.e. (1-q)N(0)+qN(1) vs (1-q)N(0)+qN(2) -- gives eps = 2.3989 for the same one step; at W=4 it is 3.1387. So the reported per-step epsilon understates a worst-case realisable one by ~12x at W=2 in this configuration, with no warning, no accountant signal, and nothing in docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md (which has no resume section at all).
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:3945-3950 -- `if self._ddp.world_size > 1: sampler_key = fold_in(sampler_key, self._ddp.rank)` (fresh-run per-rank independence)

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1871-1877 -- every rank overwrites its rank-folded template with `from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)`

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1487-1494 -- 'The accountant uses regular ``acc.poisson`` over the global rate.'

Live 2-rank gloo repro: fresh seeds {rank0: 1950457451192556855, rank1: 16528425509808239245}; resumed seeds {rank0: 1950457451192556855, rank1: 1950457451192556855} (scratchpad/ddp_resume_sampler.py)
Numerical hockey-stick at sigma=1, q=0.01, delta=1e-5: independent Poisson eps=0.1995, W=2 correlated-group pair eps=2.3989, W=4 eps=3.1387
docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md has no mention of resume, per-rank sampler snapshots, or this caveat; no runtime warning is emitted
findings.fix_sketch: Write per-rank sampler snapshots (`dp_runtime_rank<N>.pt`, unconditional of `should_save`, mirroring the existing per-rank RNG snapshot that `_save_rng_state` already writes) and restore each rank's own; or, minimally, re-apply the per-rank fold after deserialisation (`replace(restored, _stream_key=fold_in(snapshot_root, rank))` -- requires storing the pre-fold root in the snapshot so the cursor replay stays meaningful). Failing either, refuse to resume a world_size>1 run from a single-rank snapshot, or emit a loud runtime warning and stop calling the resulting epsilon a Poisson-amplified bound. Also correct the :3869-3873 comment: independence, not the marginal, is what the amplification theorem needs.

findings.title: The distributed guide documents a `ddp_shard` TrainingArguments option (and a `global` / parallel_poisson accounting mode) that does not exist; its launch example raises TypeError
findings.line: 36-44 (runnable example), 46-58 (mode table + the paragraph added by #1007)
findings.claim: `docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md` publishes `ddp_shard` as a `TrainingArguments` field, shows it in the page's only runnable launch snippet (`ddp_shard="per_rank"`), and documents two modes with different privacy accounting: `per_rank` ('disjoint shard per rank, Poisson accounting') and `global` ('full dataset per rank with rank-folded streams and `parallel_poisson` accounting'). No such argument, attribute, or branch exists anywhere in the codebase -- `grep -rn ddp_shard --include=*.py packages/` returns nothing, `TrainingArguments` has only `ddp_backend` and `ddp_timeout`, and the trainer unconditionally does `local_shard(...)` at world_size>1 (_dp_trainer.py:3909-3913) with `acc.poisson` accounting (:1492). `parallel_poisson` exists as an accounting factory (opaque.dpsgd.accounting) but no trainer path ever selects it. This is not a stale leftover of a removed feature: the option has never existed (it dates from the original DPTrainer commit 65518ae4) -- and the delta made it worse, because a624a34b (#1007) ADDED a paragraph describing `per_rank` divisibility requirements, and ba39783d (#1026, 'docs(transformers): reconcile trainer references') swept this page's neighbourhood without catching it.
findings.failure_scenario: A user following the distributed guide copies the launch snippet verbatim and gets `TypeError: TrainingArguments.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ddp_shard'` (reproduced). Worse for the reader who does not copy it: they believe a `global` mode exists in which every rank sees the full dataset and the run is priced with `parallel_poisson`, and may size their noise/epsilon expectations around a mode the trainer cannot enter -- so the page's only statement about which amplification theorem applies to multi-GPU training is unverifiable against the code.
evidence: docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md:41 `ddp_shard="per_rank",` inside the documented `TrainingArguments(...)` call; :46-58 the `## ddp_shard modes` section
`grep -rn 'ddp_shard' --include=*.py packages/` -> no matches; `[f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(TrainingArguments) if 'ddp' in f.name]` -> ['ddp_backend', 'ddp_timeout']
Reproduced: `TrainingArguments(output_dir='/tmp/x', ddp_shard='per_rank')` -> `TypeError: TrainingArguments.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ddp_shard'`
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:3893-3913 -- the world_size>1 branch always trims and `local_shard`s; there is no alternative branch
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1487-1494 -- accounting is always `acc.poisson` over the global rate

git log --oneline 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md -> ba39783d (#1026 docs reconciliation), a624a34b (#1007, which added the `per_rank` divisibility paragraph on top of the nonexistent option)
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the `ddp_shard` kwarg from the example and either delete the `## ddp_shard modes` section or rewrite it as a statement of the single implemented behaviour ('at WORLD_SIZE>1 the training population is trimmed to a multiple of WORLD_SIZE, sharded disjointly with local_shard, and accounted with acc.poisson at the global rate'). If a `global` / parallel_poisson mode is actually wanted, file it as a feature rather than documenting it as shipped.

findings.title: #1008 left the sibling `save_model` barrier untouched: a saving-rank failure there still strands peers in `barrier()`
findings.claim: fee28d2f (#1008) introduced `_distributed.checkpoint_barrier(ddp, local_error)` whose docstring says it 'Replaces plain ``barrier()`` calls that let a saving-rank failure leave peers blocked forever' (trainer/_distributed.py:234-243), and rewired the three stages of `_save_checkpoint` to use it (:5203, :5212, :5239). `save_model` -- the other rank-gated write path, which has exactly the same shape (`if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp): ... self._save_model_artifacts(target) ...` followed by a plain `_distributed.barrier(self._ddp)`) -- was not converted. It is now the only surviving `_distributed.barrier(...)` call site in the trainer.
findings.failure_scenario: All ranks call `trainer.save_model(dir)` after training (the documented usage; the barrier comment 'so non-saving ranks don't proceed before the save lands' presumes it). Rank 0's `save_pretrained` fails -- read-only or full output volume, a safetensors shared-tensor error, an NFS hiccup. REPRODUCED on 2-rank gloo with an injected `_save_model_artifacts` failure: rank 0 raised the real `RuntimeError: injected save_model artifact failure` while rank 1 blocked inside `barrier()` and only unblocked when rank 0's process exited, surfacing `RuntimeError: [gloo/transport/tcp/pair.cc:537] Read error ... Connection reset by peer` instead of any diagnostic about the save. If the caller wraps `save_model` in try/except (a natural thing to do for a best-effort final save) rank 0 stays alive and rank 1 blocks for the full store timeout. Not a privacy or numerical issue -- the cost is a hang / an unrelated gloo error in place of the clean cross-rank abort #1008 was written to provide.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:5031-5044 -- `if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp): ... self._save_model_artifacts(target) ...` then `if not _internal_call: _distributed.barrier(self._ddp)` with no try/except and no failure flag

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_distributed.py:234-243 -- checkpoint_barrier's own docstring: 'Replaces plain ``barrier()`` calls that let a saving-rank failure leave peers blocked forever'
`grep -n '_distributed.barrier(self._ddp)' _dp_trainer.py` -> only line 5044 remains; all three `_save_checkpoint` stages use checkpoint_barrier (:5203, :5212, :5239)

Live 2-rank gloo repro (scratchpad/savemodel_hang.py): rank0 'RAISED RuntimeError: injected save_model artifact failure'; rank1 'RAISED RuntimeError: [gloo ... pair.cc:537] Read error ... Connection reset by peer. This is typically caused by a remote worker hanging'
The #1008 regression test `scenario_checkpoint_save_failure` only covers `_save_checkpoint` (via an `on_save` callback); no scenario exercises `save_model`
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the `should_save` body of `save_model` in try/except and replace `_distributed.barrier(self._ddp)` with `_distributed.checkpoint_barrier(self._ddp, stage_error)` (keeping the `_internal_call` short-circuit, since `push_to_hub`'s internal save runs on one rank only). Add a `scenario_save_model_failure` alongside `scenario_checkpoint_save_failure` in packages/opaque-transformers/tests/distributed/_ddp_runner.py.
